assign.brief: Owner's design idea for ux/Dictate, 2026-10-01 (part of the same 'Clean mode' thread, see /framework/ai/2026-10-01/clean-dictate-mode/ — related but a separate, smaller piece): a new mic-state indicator to replace the current level-meter bar (`level: true`, which needs a fixed height). Owner's words, assembled from several passes: 'when you're on the page... maybe there's a kind of a darkened [state]... some visual cue that it's not listening. And then when you tap kind of like anywhere in the chat feed, it kind of unlocks it, but also turns it on... a little orange dot, the primary color, pretty small, but then kind of just grows, bounces... instead of using the levels indicator we have now... a little sphere that bounces/grows, it stays in place but fluctuates, the size of it pulses with the audio. So when the microphone is on you see the orange dot and as you speak it grows. Maybe you can tap on it. It should be pretty small so it's unobtrusive, bottom right corner maybe.' So: default state = darkened/locked (mic off), tapping anywhere in the chat feed unlocks AND turns the mic on; while live, a small dot in the site's primary color sits bottom-right, pulsing/growing in size with the live audio level (replacing the level-meter bar's job, no fixed-height bar needed), and is itself tappable (presumably to stop). Scope this as a new Widget option alongside the existing `level` meter (keep the existing one reachable, CLAUDE.md 'never destroy a viable version'), read ux/Dictate/readme.md and Widget.js/Widget.css and Dictate.js's on_meter level-reading first, propose the concrete mechanics briefly, implement, verify with a screenshot (talk into the mic, see it pulse), and land per finish-task.

decision.question: How should the pulsing-dot mic indicator work, concretely?
options: a third composer variant (new ComposerV2 class)
a new, independent Widget option (pulse: true) alongside level
decision.chose: a new, independent Widget option (pulse: true)
decision.why: the owner asked to replace what `level`'s bar does, not change send/merge behavior (that's `mode`'s job, already owned by the sibling clean-dictate-mode task) — so it is its own true/false display flag, same shape as `level`/`source`/`debug`. Mechanics: `Widget.render()` wraps `Thread` in one extra `.ux-dictate-widget-feed-wrap` box (only when `pulse`) so a darkened lock overlay and the dot can sit on top of the feed without scrolling away with it (the thread's own element scrolls, per the 2026-10-01 chat-autoscroll merge). Default = locked: a dark 'tap to talk' card covers the feed; tapping it calls `widget.start_mic()`. `Widget.Composer` sets `view.mic.on_start`/`on_stop` (plain Dictate instance hooks, already null by default) to flip the lock off/on; `on_meter` (the same smoothed 0..1 number `level` already reads) feeds `Widget.Pulse.set_level()`, which sets `--ux-dictate-widget-pulse-level` and a CSS `transform: scale()` grows the dot. Tapping the dot calls `widget.stop_mic()`. `level` and `pulse` can both be on; neither touches the other's code path. New class `Widget.Pulse`; new CSS only, nothing existing changed for `pulse: false` (every current caller).

log.msg: Built: Widget.js (Widget.prototype.pulse, Widget.Pulse class, the feed-wrap in render(), on_meter/on_start/on_stop wiring in Widget.Composer), Widget.css (.ux-dictate-widget-feed-wrap/-pulse/-pulse-lock/-pulse-dot), readme.md + doc/widget.md updated. Opt-in only (pulse: false by default) — no existing caller's behavior changes.
